goal: I am a DevOps engineer. I need to deploy and configure the system in a new execution environment. Before preparing the deployment, I need to understand which runtime environments and software artifacts are required, where the application and its data are executed and stored, and how the main runtime elements communicate with each other. I also need to identify the technologies and runtime dependencies involved in the communication between the application and the database.

views.title: Deployment view — Municipal Report Management System
views.purpose: Show the runtime environments, the artifacts they run, where the data lives and how the application reaches the database.

elements.name: Java 23
responsibilities: runs the application jar and its library jars on the classpath; provides javax.swing and java.awt for the GUI

elements.name: municipal-report-management.jar
responsibilities: single Maven build unit of the application (no <packaging> element, so the Maven default jar)
started as a desktop Swing process through a main method (HomePageGUI, UserLoginGUI and UserRegistrationGUI each define one)
needs a graphical display: the user interface is built with javax.swing and java.awt
carries META-INF/persistence.xml with persistence unit Municipal_Report_Management_System; RESOURCE_LOCAL, so the application opens its own JDBC connections (no application server or JNDI datasource)
database URL, user and password are fixed inside the packaged persistence.xml; changing them means rebuilding the artifact
JpaUtil creates one EntityManagerFactory for the persistence unit when first used (singleton), so the database is first contacted at the first persistence call
attached report images are kept as an absolute file path string in column attached_image; the image file itself is not stored in the database
GUI classes load /images/logo.png from the classpath; the repository ships no such resource (src/main/resources holds only META-INF/persistence.xml) and the code only logs 'Logo not found'

elements.name: hibernate-core
responsibilities: JPA provider (version 6.6.50.Final) that maps entities and issues the SQL

elements.name: forms_rt
responsibilities: IntelliJ GUI Designer runtime (version 7.0.3) used by the .form based screens

elements.name: MySQL
responsibilities: database server reached over TCP port 3306; the shipped default address is the loopback 127.0.0.1, i.e. the same host as the application

elements.name: reports_db
responsibilities: relational schema holding the persisted entities (users, reports, internal_notes, status_updates, notifications)
created by hand beforehand (CREATE DATABASE); tables are created and updated by Hibernate at start-up
schema managed with hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=update, so the database user needs DDL rights
user reports_user, granted on reports_db.* from host localhost only

limitations: Repository defines no node, host, container or Dockerfile: 'where it runs' is only the Java 23 and MySQL execution environments; the default JDBC host 127.0.0.1 implies the same machine.
Library artifacts are drawn as communicates edges from the application jar because the viewpoint has no 'uses' relation; they are in-process calls, not network links.
Transitive runtime dependencies (for example jakarta.persistence-api, jboss-logging, JDK modules) are not declared in pom.xml and are not drawn.
pom.xml misspells <configuretion> in maven-compiler-plugin; the plugin therefore ignores it, but the maven.compiler.* properties still apply.
pom.xml defines no jar-with-dependencies, shade or manifest main class: the library jars must be on the classpath at launch and the start class must be named explicitly.
Secondary need 'dependencies' (between code parts) is not shown as a separate view.
